task.description: Independently re-verify REQ-226's implementation against its validated design and all 8 acceptance criteria, and issue a clear recommendation on the flagged AC4/Scenario A dedup discrepancy.

result.note:
Independently re-ran all checks, trusting nothing in prior handoffs.

1. COMPILE/FORMAT/TEST (own output, PATH=asdf shims, real Postgres): `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -- clean, zero output, exit 0. `mix format --check-formatted` -- clean, zero output, exit 0. `mix test test/letflow/entities/definitions_test.exs` -- `Result: 16 passed`, 0 failures, finished in 15.1s, real DB queries observed (INSERT into repository_artifacts, artifact_versions, entity_definitions in the tenant schema; DROP SCHEMA cleanup on exit) -- not mocked.

2. DESIGN FIDELITY: module names (Letflow.Entities.EntityDefinition, Letflow.Entities.Definitions), file paths, function signatures (create_definition/2, get_definition/2, get_definition_by_name/2, list_definitions/2, activate_definition/4), migration column list/types, index names (entity_definitions_tenant_name_shape_idx, entity_definitions_tenant_inserted_id_idx, entity_definitions_content_hash_idx), FK on_delete: :restrict, Ecto.Enum status values, and the full error taxonomy (§5) all match the design verbatim -- no deviation found. artifact_kind.ex's moduledoc was correctly updated from seven-atom to eight-atom language.

3. ALL 8 ACS HAVE GENUINE TESTS -- confirmed each present in definitions_test.exs: AC1 (values/0 == 8-atom list, all 7 originals + :entity, lines ~117-133); AC2 (invalid definition -> {:error,{:validation,_}}, zero rows in ArtifactVersion/Artifact/EntityDefinition, ~142-157); AC3 (valid create -> 1 ArtifactVersion + 1 EntityDefinition row referencing it, plus get_definition/get_definition_by_name round-trip, ~167-211); AC4 (see item 4 below); AC5 (tenant A/B isolation + REQ-067 cursor pagination across 3 pages + page_size boundary + wrong_endpoint + invalid_schema_name, ~338-416); AC6 (activate_definition/4 flips status to :active and Activation.resolve/3 agrees, plus not_found case, ~423-452); AC7 (router.ex has no entity_definition reference; no routers/entity_definitions.ex file, ~460-471); AC8 (this review's own compile/test output above).

4. AC4/SCENARIO A DISCREPANCY -- independently confirmed via lib/letflow/entities/definition/shape.ex: content_hash/1 (L44-46) calls hash_via_canonicaliser(definition) on the raw document with zero field-stripping, so :name is included in the hash. logical_shape_of/1 (L61-65) explicitly Map.drops only [:display_name, :description] -- :name stays in both digests. Since create_definition/2 (definitions.ex L119) passes that same document's :name verbatim as Repository.create/2's artifact_name, two documents differing only in :name always produce different content_hash values, making design §4 Scenario A ('two different names, one shared repository_artifacts row') structurally unreachable through this pipeline -- confirmed independently, matching both ELIXIR-DEV's flag and SECURITY-REVIEWER's characterization.

RECOMMENDATION: this is a genuine spec defect in AC4, not an acceptable-as-is gap, and not an implementation bug either -- REQ-225's Shape module (out of this requirement's scope) was already validated and shipped with :name inside content_hash's scope, which is a defensible choice (name is part of a definition's actual byte-identity for artifact-store dedup purposes; only logical_shape_of has a documented rationale for stripping fields, and it doesn't strip :name either, correctly, since :name is part of the *logical* identity the UNIQUE constraint keys on). Given that, AC4's 'different name, shared hash' clause was never achievable to begin with, independent of anything ELIXIR-DEV or this design could have done differently -- REQ-226's design could not have satisfied it without REQ-225 dropping :name from content_hash, which would break REQ-225's own already-shipped/reviewed hashing contract for an REQ-226-driven reason, out of proportion to what REQ-226 needs. Concrete action: route an AC4 text correction to REQ-ANALYST/DOC-UPDATER -- strike the 'creating two distinct entity_definitions rows if names differ' clause (replace with language matching what's actually reachable and already tested: distinct names always get distinct repository_artifacts+entity_definitions rows, full stop, with no false/accidental dedup; the only same-repository_artifacts-row-multiple-definitions case is the identical-name resubmission path in Scenario B, which correctly hits the UNIQUE constraint). Do NOT reopen REQ-225/Shape to strip :name from content_hash -- that module is validated, shipped, and correct for its own actual purpose (artifact-store byte-identity dedup keyed on full content); changing it now would be scope creep in the other direction, undoing a settled design to chase an acceptance-criterion typo. This is a spec-correction item, not a code-rework item -- the shipped implementation and tests are already doing the right, achievable thing, and are honest about the gap (definitions_test.exs's own inline comment at AC4's describe block documents exactly this, which is itself good practice worth keeping as precedent).

5. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: `git diff 0cf0503d..HEAD --stat` shows exactly the claimed files: lib/letflow/entities/definitions.ex (new), lib/letflow/entities/entity_definition.ex (new), lib/letflow/repository/artifact_kind.ex (+26/-5), lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex (+3/-1, the two-line manifest registration), priv/repo/migrations/20260906000001_create_entity_definitions.exs (new), test/letflow/entities/definitions_test.exs (new), plus three handoff JSON files. No route/controller file, no REQ-227 (record-payload validation) or REQ-228 (event registration/commands) code anywhere in the diff. Clean.

6. IDIOM/OTP: no process/GenServer/gen_statem machinery anywhere in this slice (correctly so -- it's a plain Ecto-backed context module per REQ-045's process-vs-row decision, same shape as Letflow.Repository). create_definition/2 uses `case`/`with` exactly the way Letflow.Repository.create/2 does; get_definition/2 and get_definition_by_name/2 use the same nil-to-{:error,:not_found} tagged-tuple convention as Activation.resolve/3 (never Repo.get!/2 on a caller-triggerable path); list_definitions/2 mirrors list_versions/4's cursor-pagination shape (seek predicate, split-page-plus-one, ED: prefix distinct from RV:) field-for-field. Naming (Definition/EntityDefinition/Definitions three-way split) matches the Artifact/ArtifactVersion/Repository precedent exactly as the design mandated; no collapsing or ambiguous renaming occurred. tenant_id is derived from prefix in every function, never accepted as a caller-supplied field -- create_attrs's type has no tenant_id key. No supervision-integrity concern: this table is Ecto/Postgres-row-based like every other REQ-202/REQ-203 sibling, consistent with Letflow.InstanceSupervisor's deliberate emptiness (REQ-045). No scope creep: no abstractions, behaviours, or macros introduced ahead of what's needed; activate_definition/4 is exactly the 'thin wrapper' the design specified, adding no new activation mechanism (confirmed: zero new tables/pointers, only a plain Repo.update on the existing entity_definitions.status column).

7. MIGRATION IDIOM: structurally consistent with 20260830030001_create_repository_artifacts.exs -- same `if prefix() do ... schema = prefix() ... end` guard, same primary_key: false + explicit binary_id id, same explicit index-naming rationale (NAMEDATALEN collision avoidance) restated in comments, same timestamps(updated_at: false) convention, same moduledoc-style header comment block explaining placement/INV-7/immutability posture. The one deliberate divergence -- no BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE trigger -- is explicitly justified in both the migration's own header comment and design §1.4/§6 OQ-2 (no update/delete path exists yet in this requirement's scope), not a silent omission. Correctly registered in TenantProvisioning's @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest (both migration-file-creation and manifest-registration halves present, per that module's own mandatory-pairing comment).

No type-safety gap worth filing under docs/issues/ was found beyond the already-flagged AC4 spec item -- the Ecto.Enum on status and the tagged-tuple error taxonomy already make the relevant invalid states unrepresentable where it matters.

Overall: PASS. No idiom violation, no supervision-integrity regression, no scope creep, no unresolved decision-record conflict. One actionable non-blocking item: route an AC4 text correction (see recommendation above) to REQ-ANALYST rather than reworking any code.
